text:
Detective Howard stared at the file, the fluorescent lights of the precinct humming a low, irritating tune that seemed to vibrate in his teeth. Tomorrow was his last day. He had packed his box, said his goodbyes, and even bought a bottle of expensive scotch to toast a career defined by integrity. But tonight, the evidence on his desk didn't care about his retirement party. It screamed.

The fingerprints on the burner phone found in the suspect’s trunk matched his partner, Elias, perfectly. Not just the prints, but the digital trail leading back to Elias’s personal account. Elias, who had pulled him out of a burning building in '98. Elias, who had been his best man.

Howard’s hand trembled as he reached for the phone to call the internal affairs tip line. His finger hovered over the dial button. If he made this call, Elias would be arrested before sunrise. Their thirty-year friendship would be reduced to a case file, a cautionary tale told by rookies. But if he didn’t, he wasn’t just a retired cop; he was an accessory. He was complicit in the very corruption he had spent his life fighting.

The door to his office creaked open. Elias stood there, holding two cups of coffee, a warm, familiar smile on his face. "Hey, old friend. Just wanted to drop off this last pot before I head out. You look like you’ve seen a ghost."

Howard looked at the man he trusted most, then down at the evidence that would destroy him. The air in the room suddenly felt thin, suffocating. He had to choose: loyalty to the brother he had chosen, or loyalty to the badge he had worn.

A lemon.
